_provenance.reconstruction_note: This fixture is RECONSTRUCTED from two real historical sources — it is NOT a saved raw API response captured verbatim at request time. Every field below traces to one of those two sources; field_provenance_key explains the label on each entry. A SEPARATE test (test_kraken_ccxt_adapter_contract.py) verifies the installed ccxt library's REAL parsing behavior against an independently-defined raw payload, since this fixture's shape and KrakenFixtureSource's parser were authored together and cannot validate each other.

sources.reconciliation_report: logs/reconciliation_20260703.md — output of a real reconcile_ledger.py run against the live Kraken account, 2026-07-03T02:15:05Z. Its own trade table is DISPLAY-ROUNDED to 4 decimal places.
sources.trades_db: logs/trades.db — the bot's own real historical SQLite fills table, same account/window. Stores higher-precision floats than the report's rounded table, and its 'notes' column captured the real Kraken trade id for 6 of the 7 BTC/CAD trades used here (via reconcile_ledger.py's backfill step, 2026-07-03).

field_provenance_key.captured: an exact Kraken trade id, literally recorded in trades.db's notes column
field_provenance_key.db_recorded: trades.db's own stored float for that fill — higher precision than the report's rounded table, but still the BOT's OWN recorded value, not a saved raw API payload
field_provenance_key.report_value: the value in reconciliation_20260703.md's own trade table, sourced from a real fetch_my_trades() call but printed there already rounded to 4 decimal places
field_provenance_key.placeholder: no real value exists in either source; a clearly-marked stand-in, never presented as captured
field_provenance_key.normalized: a ccxt-unified value (e.g. symbol 'BTC/CAD') — Kraken's own RAW internal pair id (e.g. an 'XXBTZCAD'-style code) is not captured anywhere in this repository and is not reconstructed here; see the ccxt-adapter contract test for real raw-pair behavior instead

trades_history._shape_note: Mirrors ccxt.kraken.fetch_my_trades's real raw response shape: result.trades is a dict keyed by the Kraken trade transaction id, each value carrying ordertxid/pair/time/type/ordertype/price/cost/fee/vol — confirmed against the installed ccxt==4.5.56 source this session. Every trade here uses the EXCHANGE's own true values (report_value or db_recorded from a captured trade id) — none of the bot's own local-ledger errors are mixed into this section; see local_ledger_error below for that, kept separate on purpose.

TRLSTP-PLACEHOLDER-ID._id_note: reconciliation_20260703.md never printed this fill's real Kraken trade id (matched by price/time proximity, not by id) — no id for it exists in either real source used by this fixture. price/cost/fee are the EXCHANGE's real true values from the report's own trade table (section 1, row 6) — these are NOT the bot's local trades.db values, which are wrong; see local_ledger_error below for that comparison.

local_ledger_error._note: NOT exchange data. This is the bot's OWN pre-existing, real historical trades.db row (id=1) for the SAME fill as trades_history's TRLSTP-PLACEHOLDER-ID entry above, written by the live bot BEFORE reconcile_ledger.py ever ran against this account — a genuine, real local-ledger bug (predates the 2026-08-26 post-only-param fix documented in CLAUDE.md). Used by the fee-correction integration test to model a pre-existing local record being brought in line with a freshly-observed exchange trade — never framed as 'the exchange revised its fee'.

external_holdings_incident._note: The real 2026-06-27 external-holdings bug (reconciliation_20260703.md section 9): a pre-existing BTC deposit (not bot-bought) was sold by the bot due to a stale state flag, before the ADOPT_EXTERNAL_HOLDINGS guard existed. trade_id is the REAL captured Kraken trade id (trades.db row id=9's notes column) -- not a placeholder.
